Title: BEETHOVEN - Symphony No. 9 | @sydneysymphony  | Digital Season
Description:
The Ninth Symphony is considered one of Beethoven’s greatest works and the ‘Ode to Joy’ theme of the final movement is one of the most widely recognised melodies in classical music. Former Chief Conductor Edo de Waart returned to lead the orchestra in the performance, which also features Sydney Philharmonia Choirs and American soprano Amanda Majeski making her Australian debut.

LUDWIG VAN BEETHOVEN (1770–1827)
Symphony No.9 in D minor, Op.125 (Choral)
0:30 I. Allegro, ma non troppo, un poco maestoso
16:10 II. Molto vivace – Presto
28:54 III. Adagio molto e cantabile – Andante moderato
42:50  IV. Allegro assai (Choral Finale on Schiller’s Ode To Joy)

Amanda Majeski, soprano
Caitlin Hulcup, mezzo-soprano
Kim Begley, tenor
Shenyang, bass-baritone
Sydney Philharmonia Choirs

Title: Earth Cry | Peter Sculthorpe | ABBL Orchestra | Conductor: Simone Young AM
Description:
Recorded live at the Australian Bushfire Benefit London concert on Sunday 1st March 2020 in Duke's Hall, Royal Academy of Music. 

In the presence of the High Commissioner of Australia to the United Kingdom, His Excellency the Honourable George Brandis QC

Earth Cry (1986)*
Composer: Peter Sculthorpe
ABBL Orchestra
Conductor: Simone Young AM

Formed by Australian musicians in London who produced a concert featuring Australia’s finest musicians with full orchestra and choir to honour the brave men and women who fought the worst fires in Australia’s history. Our hearts are with the people of Australia and we hope that the money raised from this concert will make a tangible difference to the victims of this horrific tragedy.

* Performed and recorded with the permission of Faber Music Ltd

Financial Assistance for Artists affected by the COVID-19 crisis

The Tait Memorial Trust has established an Emergency Relief Fund for Australia/New Zealand Artists to assist our talented young artists who overnight lost 6 months or more of work. Professional artists, some with losses in excess of £40,000, to artists just out of college who had a regular income of £500 to 3,000 per month which has now disappeared. Most, but thankfully not all, of the performing arts companies are claiming force majeur and leaving our awardees with an uncertain future. Currently many of them can’t get any assistance from the U.K. government stimulus package because they are self employed, nor do they qualify for Universal Credit because they are here on restricted visas and have no access to public funds.

Description:

Erich Wolfgang Korngold - Sinfonie in Fis op. 40

00:00:00 I. Moderato ma energico – Allegro – Tempo I
00:15:42 II. Scherzo. Allegro molto – Trio. Molto meno (tranquillo) – Tempo I
00:26:04 III. Adagio. Lento
00:40:48 IV. Finale. Allegro – Più lento – Tempo I (poco meno)

WDR Sinfonieorchester

► Werkbetrachtung mit Simone Young: Korngolds Sinfonie in Fis zeigt, wie viele Facetten der Komponist hatte. Simone Young erzählt im Video, was sie an der Sinfonie so fasziniert und nach welcher Farbe die Sinfonie für sie klingt: https://youtu.be/KUhP6YM0q-Y

► Mehr zum Sinfonieorchester, zu Konzerten und aktuellen Livestreams gibt es bei https://sinfonieorchester.wdr.de 
► Das WDR Sinfonieorchester bei Facebook   / wdrsinfonieorchester  
► Weitere Konzerte und Werkeinführungen aus der Welt der klassischen Musik, Symphonic Crossover, Chorgesang und Konzerte für Kinder finden sie auch in der ARD Mediathek: https://www.ardmediathek.de/klassik

Werkeinführung
Anfang der 1930er Jahre ist Erich Wolfgang Korngold einer der erfolgreichsten Komponisten auf deutschsprachigen Opernbühnen. Seine Karriere hätte nicht steiler verlaufen können. Geboren 1897 in Brünn, schrieb Gustav Mahler schon über den Zwölfjährigen ungläubig: »ein Genie!«. Korngold ist gerade einmal 13 Jahre alt, als sein erstes Ballett an der Wiener Hofoper gegeben wird. Zehn Jahre später reißen sich die Opernhäuser um die Uraufführung seiner Oper »Die tote Stadt«. Korngold landet damit einen Sensationserfolg. Zur Zeit der Weimarer Republik ist er einer der größten Konkurrenten von Richard Strauss.

Doch mit der Machtergreifung der Nationalsozialisten sind Aufführungen von Korngolds Musik mit einem Schlag verboten. In dieser prekären Lage ist ein Angebot aus Hollywood sein Rettungsanker: Der legendäre Regisseur Max Reinhardt ist aus Berlin in die USA geflohen und verfilmt dort 1934 Shakespeares »Ein Sommernachtstraum«. Und Korngold soll die Musik dazu beisteuern. Der Erfolg seiner ersten Filmmusik macht den Österreicher zum Star der Branche. Mit seiner überbordenden Orchesterpalette prägt er den klangmächtigen Hollywood-Sound bis heute. Zu rund zwanzig Filmen schreibt Korngold die Musik, gewinnt Ende der 1930er Jahre zweimal den Oscar. Aber dann, nach 1945, versucht er, wieder in Österreich und Deutschland Fuß zu fassen – nun mit Orchestermusik für den Konzertsaal. Er muss jedoch die Erfahrung machen, dass sein spätromantischer Stil von den Entscheidungsträgern als veraltet vom Tisch gefegt wird. An seine früheren Erfolge kann er nicht mehr anknüpfen.

Auf einer Europareise stellt er dem Wiener Publikum 1954 seine Sinfonie in Fis vor. Eruptiv ist diese Musik, hochemotional, zwischen geballten Orchesterentladungen und Linien einzelner Instrumente hin und her pendelnd. Noch ganz und gar typisch der heroische Korngold-Ton – aber unverkennbar einer, der die Erinnerung an das Grauen des Zweiten Weltkriegs in sich trägt.

(Text: Otto Hagedorn)

Erich Wolfgang Korngold's Symphony in F sharp, played by the WDR Symphony Orchestra under the direction of Simone Young. Recorded live on 06.02.2026 at the Cologne Philharmonic.

Erich Wolfgang Korngold - Symphony in F sharp op. 40

00:00:00 I. Moderato ma energico – Allegro – Tempo I
00:15:42 II. Scherzo. Allegro molto – Trio. Molto meno (tranquillo) – Tempo I
00:26:04 III. Lento

WDR Symphony Orchestra
Simone Young, conductor

► Reflection on the work with Simone Young: Korngold's Symphony in F sharp shows how many facets the composer had. In the video, Simone Young tells us what fascinates her so much about the symphony and what color the symphony sounds like to her: https://youtu.be/KUhP6YM0q-Y

► More about the symphony orchestra, concerts and current livestreams can be found at https://sinfonieorchester.wdr.de 
► The WDR Symphony Orchestra on Facebook / wdrsinfonieorchester  
► Further concerts and introductions to works from the world of classical music, symphonic crossover, choral singing and concerts for children can also be found in the ARD Mediathek: https://www.ardmediathek.de/klassik

Introduction to the work
At the beginning of the 1930s, Erich Wolfgang Korngold was one of the most successful composers on German-language opera stages. His career could not have been steeper. Born in Brno in 1897, Gustav Mahler wrote incredulously about the twelve-year-old: "a genius!" Korngold was just 13 years old when his first ballet was given at the Vienna Court Opera. Ten years later, the opera houses are scrambling for the world premiere of his opera »The Dead City«. Korngold thus lands a sensational success. At the time of the Weimar Republic, he was one of Richard Strauss's biggest competitors.

But with the seizure of power by the National Socialists, performances of Korngold's music were banned in one fell swoop. In this precarious situation, an offer from Hollywood is his lifeline: the legendary director Max Reinhardt has fled from Berlin to the USA and is filming Shakespeare's »A Midsummer Night's Dream« there in 1934. And Korngold is to contribute the music. The success of his first film score makes the Austrian a star of the industry. With his exuberant orchestral palette, he still shapes the powerful Hollywood sound today. Korngold wrote the music for around twenty films and won two Oscars at the end of the 1930s. But then, after 1945, he tried to regain a foothold in Austria and Germany – now with orchestral music for the concert hall. However, he has to make the experience that his late Romantic style is swept off the table by the decision-makers as outdated. He can no longer build on his earlier successes.

On a trip to Europe in 1954, he presented his Symphony in F sharp to the Viennese audience. This music is eruptive, highly emotional, oscillating back and forth between concentrated orchestral discharges and lines of individual instruments. The heroic Korngold tone is still quite typical – but unmistakably one that carries the memory of the horror of the Second World War.

(Text: Otto Hagedorn)
